title: Wheelchair-accessible routing in Brussels
summary: Comparing A*, constraint filtering and MDP planning on OpenStreetMap graphs enriched with slope, width, curb and surface data.
role: Academic project · map pipeline, graph attributes, benchmark
metrics: routes found by A* and MDP
tldr: Plans routes that respect a maximum slope (8%) and minimum width (1.2 m), with a controlled fallback when no route exists.
I built the shared map pipeline, graph attributes, configuration and benchmark integration.
facts: Map pipeline, edge attributes, configuration, benchmark integration
Fatima Ben Mostefa, Francesca Grasso, Lara Moreno, Matteo Paolini

sections.title: Pipeline
body: The pipeline geocodes the endpoints, downloads only the area around them (500 m margin) and caches the graph. Edges are enriched with slope, width, curb, surface and wheelchair tags. If no route satisfies the constraints, the area grows and the limits relax to 15% slope and 1.0 m width, while absolute exclusions stay in place.

sections.title: Results
body: On eight Brussels scenarios A* and the MDP planner found routes in all eight, the CSP planner in seven. Interactive maps make each comparison inspectable.
